The Big Question

💻 You can have the best hardware… but without software it does nothing.

What actually makes a computer usable?

❌ Common misconception...

"Software just means apps."

✅ System software runs the computer.

The OS, drivers, and utilities manage hardware so applications can work.

Two Families of Software

System Software

Programs that manage the computer's hardware and provide a platform for applications.

  • Operating System (OS)
  • Utilities (Antivirus)
  • Drivers
  • Translators (Compilers)

Application Software

Programs that allow the user to perform specific tasks.

  • Word Processor
  • Spreadsheet
  • Games
  • Web Browser
Deep Dive: Application Examples

Application Software Examples

Word Processor
Manipulate text, format documents (Word, Docs).
Spreadsheet
Organize numbers, formulas, graphs (Excel, Sheets).
Database
Store, query, and analyze data (Access, SQL).
Control
Interface with sensors to control devices.
Photo Editing
Manipulate digital images (Photoshop).
Video Editing
Cut, arrange, and enhance video clips.

Check Your Understanding

A Web Browser allows you to access the internet. Which category is it?

A) System Software
B) Application Software

B) Application Software

It is a tool you choose to use to perform a specific task (browsing).

The Operating System (OS)

Operating system software runs in the background to manage basic functions and provide a platform for applications.

Examples: Windows, macOS, Linux, Android, iOS.

Deep Dive: OS Functions

Key Functions of the OS

1. HCI
Human Computer Interface (GUI/CLI).
2. Memory Mgmt
Allocates RAM to programs.
3. Multitasking
Shares CPU time between processes.
4. Security
Logins, passwords, permissions.
5. File Mgmt
Save, delete, move files.
6. Hardware
Manages peripherals via Drivers.

Deep Dive: HCI

CLI (Command Line)

  • Type commands.
  • Fast, low memory.
  • Hard to learn.
  • Used by technicians.

GUI (Graphical)

  • WIMP (Windows, Icons, Menus, Pointers).
  • Easy to use (intuitive).
  • Uses more memory.
  • Used by everyday users.

Quick Check

Which OS function allocates RAM to programs?

Memory management

Did You Know?

“Boot”

“Booting” comes from bootstrapping — starting the computer using a tiny program in ROM.

The OS is then loaded into RAM so it can run.

Android

Android uses a Linux-based kernel.

That’s why ideas like processes and permissions appear across many OSes.

Utility Software

Programs that help manage, maintain, and control computer resources.

Virus Checkers
Scan for malware, quarantine infected files.
Defragmentation
Reorganize files on HDD to speed up access.
Backup
Create copies of data (Local or Cloud).
Security
Firewalls, Encryption.
Screensavers
Prevent screen burn (old) or lock screen (security).

Interrupts

Interrupt = a signal sent to the CPU to pause the current process and handle a high‑priority task.

Why? To allow multitasking and handle hardware events (e.g., printer out of paper).
Deep Dive: The Process

The Interrupt Process

1. Normal Operation
CPU is executing a program.
2. Interrupt Signal
A device (e.g., Printer) sends a signal.
3. Pause
CPU pauses current task. Saves state (registers) to stack.
4. Service
CPU runs the Interrupt Service Routine (ISR).
5. Resume
CPU restores saved state and continues original task.

Buffers

How do we handle speed differences?

The Problem

CPU is super fast. Printer is slow.

The Solution: Buffer

A temporary memory area. CPU fills the buffer, then goes back to work. Printer empties the buffer slowly.

Link: When buffer is empty -> Interrupt sent to CPU to refill it.

Quick Check

What is the first thing the CPU does when an interrupt happens?

Save the current state (e.g., register contents) so it can resume later.

Q2: Identify the Utility

Which utility reorganizes files on the disk to speed up access?

Defragmentation

It moves file blocks to be contiguous.

Q3: Interrupts

What happens to the current task when an interrupt occurs?

It is Paused

Its state is saved, the interrupt is serviced, then it resumes.

True or False?

Answer these misconception checks in your book:

  1. "Application software can run without any system software."
  2. "Interrupts stop the current task permanently."
  3. "Defragmentation is a utility that can speed up disk access."

Press Down to reveal answers

Question 1

"Application software can run without any system software."

Answer: False

Applications rely on the OS, drivers, and utilities to access hardware resources.

Question 2

"Interrupts stop the current task permanently."

Answer: False

The CPU services the interrupt, restores the saved state, and resumes the original task.

Question 3

"Defragmentation is a utility that can speed up disk access."

Answer: True

It reorganises files so they are stored contiguously, reducing seek time.

Key Takeaways

🧩 System software runs the computer (OS, utilities, drivers).

🛠️ Application software helps users do tasks (browser, word processor).

🧠 The OS manages memory, files, security, and devices.

⏸️ Interrupts pause the CPU so urgent events can be handled.

📦 Buffers smooth speed differences (CPU vs printer).

🔁 After servicing an interrupt, the CPU resumes the paused program.
